brief:
Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton urged Israel to permit aid deliveries into Gaza on Wednesday, according to Al-Monitor, one day after visiting the Rafah border crossing on the Egyptian side. Hamilton's statement followed his firsthand observation of the crossing, a critical humanitarian entry point for assistance to the enclave.

The seven-time world champion did not elaborate on specific conditions he witnessed or propose particular measures for increasing aid flow during his visit to the frontier.
dek: Nov 11 (Reuters) - Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton said on Wednesday that Israel must allow aid trucks into Gaza, a day after he visited the Rafah border crossing in Egypt.
title: Hamilton calls on Israel to open Gaza aid routes after Rafah visit
